items.title: Canonical spherical structure of a pseudo-unitary fusion category
items.difficulty_reason: Given the fourth-dual tensor isomorphism and the pointwise squared-norm equality, the author analyzes the operators on each fusion multiplicity space obtained from a natural square root. These are involutions. Their trace bounds and the FP dimension character make the full triangle inequality an equality, so relative trace phases have real ratios whenever a simple summand occurs. Squaring these phases defines a tensor automorphism of the identity. Twisting the fourth-dual map by it and taking the indicated square root makes every trace positive; the fusion trace identity then forces every involution to be the identity. This coupled saturation and phase adjustment is the new H2 mechanism.

source_roles.source_scope: Original complex pseudo-unitary fusion category. Preserve existence and uniqueness of the spherical pivotal structure whose categorical dimension agrees with FPdim on every simple object.
source_roles.source_label_caveats: The last parenthetical σ_X=id_X refers to recomputing the phase after normalizing the traces. The printed sentence about T=N characterizes pivotality for the family of all triples; the previous paragraph gives this family quantifier. Sphericality is the direct simple-dual dimension test already given in Definition 4.7.14. The source does not separately spell out uniqueness: a natural transformation on a semisimple category is determined on simples, and each simple Hom(X,X**) is one dimensional with nonzero trace by 4.8.4. These are routine source-context checks, not changes to the author proof.
source_roles.norm_support_verification: The original setup already states |X|²=|d_X|². For qualification, this is a routine check using the printed pivotalization with simple (X,a_X), the actual pivotal formula |X|²=d_X d_{X*} and preservation of the norm in 7.21.12. A dimension character of the complex fusion ring with its original positive *-algebra structure has d_{X*}=conj(d_X): by 3.7.3 a one-dimensional character is projection to a one-dimensional matrix factor with conjugation. Equivalently use the simultaneous eigenvector and transpose identity already written in 7.21.12. This does not depend on sphericality of the pivotalization (7.21.10) or its problematic 7.21.8 citation. The printed final sphericality check uses positive dimensions FPdim(X)=FPdim(X*).
source_roles.official_corrections_only: Retain the separate p5 [1097,1170) correction solely for 7.21.12, no direct §9.5 entry.
